title: Research Methodology
subtitle: Probabilistic forecasting of international football outcomes using temporally valid measures of team strength, recent performance, match context, and squad market value.

sections.label: Abstract
sections.title: Abstract
paragraphs: This study formulates international football forecasting as a three-class probabilistic prediction problem over Team A win, draw, and Team B win outcomes. All covariates are constructed on a point-in-time basis from information available strictly prior to the fixture and comprise Elo ratings, recent match performance, rest intervals, venue status, and a proxy for squad market value. The principal specification is an XGBoost classifier estimated on international matches from 1990 onward. Predictive performance is assessed on a chronological holdout of 2,245 competitive fixtures played from 2023 onward, using multiclass log loss as the primary scoring rule and constant-prior and Elo-based multinomial logistic models as benchmarks. For neutral-site fixtures, predictions are symmetrized across both possible home/away slot assignments to eliminate dependence on arbitrary team ordering. On the holdout sample, the 17-feature XGBoost specification attains a log loss of 0.8327, compared with 0.8355 for the Elo-logistic benchmark. The paired bootstrap confidence interval for the difference spans zero; accordingly, the estimated improvement is small and cannot be distinguished statistically from no improvement at the 95% confidence level.

sections.label: Problem Formulation
sections.title: Problem Formulation and Outcome Definition
paragraphs: For fixture i between two national teams, conditional on venue status, the forecasting function returns the probability vector p_i = (p_{i,A}, p_{i,D}, p_{i,B}), corresponding to a Team A victory, draw, and Team B victory. Historical observations are represented using nominal home and away slots (classes 0, 1, and 2). This ordering is substantively meaningful for non-neutral fixtures but arbitrary for neutral-site matches; predictions for the latter are therefore symmetrized with respect to slot assignment.

The dependent variable records the terminal match outcome rather than the result after regulation time. Fixtures resolved in extra time or by penalty shootout are assigned to the eventual winner, whereas the draw class is reserved for matches that conclude without a winner, including group-stage fixtures and friendlies. Consequently, the response variable is not homogeneous across competition formats: it represents a match result when a draw is admissible and an advancement outcome when the competition requires a winner. This distinction is especially important for interpretation of the draw probability, because the draw class is structurally unavailable in such knockout fixtures.

The empirical objective is probability estimation rather than deterministic classification. Draws constitute approximately one quarter of international fixtures, yet need not be the modal class even when the associated probability is well calibrated. A single pooled model is estimated across national teams. Team-pair-specific models are avoided because head-to-head histories are typically sparse, and team identity is not entered directly as a covariate.

callouts.title: Outcome coding
callouts.body: Draws are admissible only for fixtures that may terminate level. Knockout fixtures requiring a winner are coded according to the eventual winner after extra time or penalties; for such observations, the draw class is structurally unavailable.

callouts.title: Notation and loss function
callouts.body:
Let x_i ∈ ℝ^d be features for match i.
Let y_i be the one-hot outcome; f(x_i; θ) outputs p_i with Σ p = 1.

Minimize L(θ) = −(1/N) Σ [ y^H log p^H + y^D log p^D + y^A log p^A ]

sections.label: Data
sections.title: Data Sources and Sample Construction
paragraphs: Match-level outcomes are obtained from the martj42/international_results repository. The results.csv file reports match scores, including extra-time scores but excluding penalty-shootout outcomes; these records are joined to shootouts.csv to recover shootout winners. Following preprocessing, the resulting database contains 49,405 fixtures played between 1872-11-30 and 2026-06-11 across 336 national teams, of which 677 are associated with a shootout winner.

Sample construction is implemented in download_data.py. Fixtures with missing scores are removed as unplayed observations, team names are harmonized through an alias map, duplicate records are identified on the composite key (date, home, away), and shootout winners are merged using the same key. These operations define the canonical match table used by the downstream feature pipeline.

Model estimation uses observations dated 1990-01-01 or later. Earlier fixtures are nevertheless retained when recursively constructing Elo ratings so that post-1990 ratings reflect the available pre-sample history. Squad market-value information is drawn from transfermarkt-datasets (players and valuations) and converted into quarterly point-in-time snapshots beginning in 2004.

sections.label: Feature Engineering
sections.title: Covariate Construction
paragraphs: To prevent temporal leakage, every predictor is evaluated strictly as of the date preceding the target fixture. No feature incorporates information from the fixture being predicted or from any later observation.

Team strength is represented primarily through Elo ratings initialized at 1500. For non-neutral fixtures, 100 rating points are added to the nominal home side, and updates use match-type-specific K factors of 60, 50, 40, 30, or 20 following the convention reported by eloratings.net. Penalty shootouts are treated as draws for the purpose of Elo updating, because the rating update is based on the on-field scoreline; the supervised target is defined differently and records the shootout winner.

Recent performance is summarized over each team's preceding five and ten fixtures. Separate features are retained for points, goal difference, goals scored, and goals conceded, allowing recent attacking and defensive performance to enter independently rather than through a single aggregate form measure. The feature vector also includes days since each team's previous fixture and an indicator for neutral venue.

Squad strength is proxied by the aggregate market value of the 25 highest-valued players associated with a given citizenship. For each player, the latest valuation observed within the preceding 18 months is used, and the resulting team-level quantity is transformed using log1p. Because valuation records begin in 2004, squad features are missing for earlier observations; these values remain NaN and are handled natively by XGBoost. The measure should be interpreted as an imperfect proxy for available playing strength: citizenship does not coincide exactly with FIFA eligibility, dual nationals and fringe selections are only partially represented, and valuation coverage is more complete for players active in European leagues.
The selected model contains 17 predictors. Squad-value covariates are retained, whereas the competitive-match indicator is omitted following the ablation analysis described below.

sections.label: Models
sections.title: Predictive Models
paragraphs: Two benchmark models are estimated to provide reference levels of predictive performance. The constant-prior benchmark assigns every fixture the empirical class distribution observed in the training sample. The second benchmark is a multinomial logistic regression using standardized elo_diff as its sole predictor. The Elo-logistic model constitutes the more substantive benchmark because it tests whether the richer covariate set and nonlinear functional form yield predictive gains beyond a conventional measure of relative team strength.

The principal model is XGBClassifier with the multi:softprob objective. The specification sets max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.1, n_estimators=300, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, and random_state=42. These hyperparameters were not selected through a separate optimization procedure; the reported analysis therefore evaluates a fixed specification rather than a comprehensively tuned XGBoost model.

For neutral-site fixtures, nominal home/away assignment introduces an arbitrary representation that should not affect the resulting probabilities. Each neutral fixture is therefore evaluated under both possible slot orderings. In the mirrored representation, home- and away-win probabilities are exchanged, all *_diff covariates change sign, and slot-specific variables are swapped. The two aligned probability vectors are then averaged. This symmetrization is applied identically during holdout evaluation and subsequent prediction.

cards.title: Symmetrization
cards.body: Neutral-site probabilities are averaged across both aligned slot orderings to enforce invariance to arbitrary home/away assignment.

sections.label: Evaluation
sections.title: Temporal Evaluation Design
paragraphs: Predictive performance is evaluated using a chronological split. Fixtures dated from 1990-01-01 through 2022-12-31 constitute the estimation sample, while fixtures from 2023-01-01 onward constitute the holdout period. Reported comparisons are restricted to the 2,245 competitive fixtures in the holdout, reflecting the intended 2026 World Cup application domain. All candidate specifications are evaluated on this identical set of observations.

Multiclass log loss is used as the primary evaluation criterion because the object of interest is the full predictive distribution rather than the modal class alone. Brier score and classification accuracy are reported as secondary diagnostics. Accuracy is comparatively limited in this setting: draws account for roughly 25% of fixtures, and a calibrated draw probability need not be the largest of the three class probabilities. Sampling uncertainty is quantified by 1,000 bootstrap resamples, from which 95% confidence intervals are obtained for model-specific log loss and for paired differences in log loss between specifications.

The holdout period should not be interpreted as a fully untouched test sample. It was used to compare a small, prespecified set of four model configurations, introducing some model-selection dependence into the reported estimates and, therefore, a modest risk of optimistic bias. A stricter evaluation design would perform specification selection by rolling-origin validation and reserve the 2023+ period for a single final assessment.

sections.label: Experiments
sections.title: Ablation and Model Comparison
paragraphs: Four prespecified configurations are compared on the common 2,245-match holdout. The specification retained for subsequent use is estimated on all available training matches and includes 17 predictors, retaining the squad-value variables while excluding the competitive-match indicator. Following model selection, this specification is re-estimated on all 32,288 matches observed from 1990 through 2026-06-11. The refitted model is used only for subsequent prediction; all performance statistics reported here are derived from the earlier chronological holdout evaluation.

tables.caption: Table 3: Experiment grid (shared 2,245-match competitive test set)

findings: Restricting estimation to competitive fixtures yields a log loss of 0.8444, compared with 0.8343 or lower for otherwise comparable specifications trained on the broader match sample.

Excluding the squad-value covariates increases log loss from 0.8327 to 0.8387 (Δ = 0.0060), providing evidence that the valuation proxy contributes incremental predictive information in this specification.
Including the competitive-match indicator changes log loss only marginally (0.8343 versus 0.8327); the indicator is therefore excluded from the selected 17-feature specification.

Relative to the Elo-logistic benchmark, XGBoost reduces log loss by 0.0028. The 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the paired difference is [−0.0119, 0.0072], which includes zero and does not provide evidence of a statistically distinguishable improvement at the 95% confidence level.

sections.label: Calibration & Errors
sections.title: Calibration and Error Decomposition
paragraphs: Calibration diagnostics indicate that home- and away-win probabilities broadly track empirical frequencies over most of the probability range, with mild overconfidence in home-win predictions between approximately 0.5 and 0.9. Predicted draw probabilities do not exceed approximately 0.40. Within the 0.2–0.3 draw-probability bin, the mean predicted probability and empirical draw frequency are both 0.248, whereas larger discrepancies are concentrated in the tails. These residual departures motivate consideration of a goals-based specification, such as a Poisson model, for future treatment of draw probabilities.

Prediction error is concentrated disproportionately among closely matched teams. Fixtures with an Elo gap below 150 exhibit materially larger log loss than fixtures with greater rating separation. The draw class also illustrates the distinction between probabilistic calibration and argmax classification: draw probabilities may be well aligned with empirical frequencies even when the draw is rarely the most probable class. Conditional on an observed draw, argmax classification accuracy is 2.0%.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.title: Limitations and Directions for Further Research
paragraphs: Several features of the empirical design qualify the interpretation of the results. First, the dependent variable combines fixtures in which a draw is an admissible terminal outcome with knockout fixtures that must produce a winner; in the latter case, extra time and penalty shootouts enter the outcome definition. A formulation that models regulation-time scorelines separately from advancement would provide a cleaner separation of these processes. Second, the squad-value variable is a coarse proxy for realized squad strength. It is affected by dual nationality, the imperfect correspondence between citizenship and FIFA eligibility, and uneven valuation coverage across leagues. Third, the predictive gain of XGBoost over the Elo-logistic benchmark is small, and the paired bootstrap interval includes zero. The analysis also does not include systematic hyperparameter optimization, while the tiered Elo K factors are adopted from established convention rather than estimated within the present framework. Finally, venue is represented only by a binary home/neutral distinction, so quasi-home effects are not modeled, and FIFA rankings are omitted on the assumption that they are largely redundant with Elo in the post-2018 period.
findings: Model regulation-time scorelines separately from conditional advancement in knockout fixtures.
Evaluate a Poisson goals model as an alternative probabilistic treatment of draw outcomes.
Recompute ratings and time-varying covariates after each matchday during tournament deployment.
Introduce SHAP-based local attribution and rolling-origin cross-validation for specification selection.

sections.label: Reproducibility
sections.title: Computational Reproducibility
paragraphs: The computational workflow is organized under pipeline/ into four stages: data acquisition, feature construction, model estimation, and prediction. All stochastic components are seeded with random_state=42. Model diagnostics and evaluation artifacts—including point estimates, bootstrap confidence intervals, calibration outputs, permutation importance, error-stratified results, and example predictions—are persisted in models/model_meta.json. A separate development record in docs/DEVLOG.md documents implementation changes and methodological decisions made during construction of the pipeline.
